competitive_landscape: Local ferries (CTN, SNTRI ground links) cover the Ajim–Jorf and Sfax–Kerkennah lanes; tourist boats are fragmented and seasonal. Nothing premium, nothing electric. Cross-border (Sicily, Malta) is freight-led with no fast passenger operator — Quanta corridors are wide open but partner-dependent.

navier_fit.pioneer_ii: Pioneer II covers the local Tunisian short hops — Ajim↔Jorf (~2 nm), Houmt Souk↔Kerkennah (~50 nm), Djerba coastal resort loops — all inside the 70 nm all-electric envelope on protected Gulf water.
navier_fit.quanta_lr: Hybrid Quanta-LR is a longer-horizon Central-Med option — Tunisia↔Sicily (~150 nm) and Tunisia↔Malta (~150 nm) — with no charging-infrastructure dependency. Activates only once cross-border partner channels exist.

precedents.why_it_matters: Dense short-hop archipelago electrification proves the inter-island playbook that Djerba + Kerkennah can plug into longer-horizon — once cross-border partner channels exist.

regulatory_note: Med SOx-ECA technically applies but Tunisian enforcement is materially softer than EU FuelEU Maritime. Djerba's UNESCO 2023 listing layers heritage / quiet-mode arguments. Cross-border (Tunisia↔Sicily / Malta) requires EU Schengen and Tunisian maritime customs coordination — a partner-coordination question rather than a regulatory blocker.
seasonality: Mediterranean-North-African — peak April–June and September–November (beach season avoiding peak heat), with year-round Ajim–Jorf commuter base. Winter operability is good on protected Gulf water; only the long Central-Med Quanta legs see exposure.

summary: Djerba is Tunisia's largest island, a flat sandy resort island in the shallow Gulf of Gabes. Its main marina is at Houmt Souk on the north shore, while the Ajim ferry port on the west point is the island's historic link to the mainland. Water routes here must thread the extensive Djerba sandbanks, making a shallow-draft fast shuttle a natural fit for island and mainland connections.
tagline: Tunisia's UNESCO-listed island anchor — the only North-African Western-Med candidate; watch-leaning standard until network depth arrives.
